title: How Stamp Collecting Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore stamp collecting (philately): why it is a low-cost, personal hobby, common jargon (gum, blocks, errors/freaks/oddities, cancelations, covers, perforations, salvage, caches), how to start (tongs, albums, perf gauge, watermark detector fluid, grab bags, pen pals) and how to soak stamps off envelopes. They cover stamp history starting with Britain's Penny Black (May 1840), the US first stamps in 1847, the Scott Catalog and Michel Catalog, famous collectors (including FDR, John Lennon, Amelia Earhart's covers, Sally Ride), and the Inverted Jenny error stamp and its thefts. The episode closes with a listener email from Zeneida Johnson about pandemic-era listening.

segments.title: Opening banter and stamp collecting introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the episode, joke about their collecting pasts (baseball cards, piggy banks), and introduce stamp collecting and the term philately.

segments.title: Stamp collecting as a hobby and its low cost
segments.summary: The hosts discuss that most stamps are not valuable, that collectors prize stamps used on mail, and that the Scott Catalog only recognizes government-issued postage stamps.
topics: collecting for love of the hobby

segments.title: Stamp collecting jargon: gum, blocks, errors, cancelations, covers
segments.summary: Definitions of common philatelic terms including gum, blocks, errors/freaks/oddities, cancelations, and covers, along with the idea of collecting postmarks like disaster-date cancelations.

segments.title: Perforations, salvage, and Henry Archer
segments.summary: The hosts explain perforations, Henry Archer's perforating tool, the first perforated stamp (Penny Red, 1850), imperforate stamps, and salvage margins.

segments.title: Getting started: tools, albums, and grab bags
segments.summary: Recommended beginner gear: tongs, stamp albums and hinges, magnifier, perforation gauge, watermark detector fluid and light projector, plus buying grab bags and getting free stamps or pen pals.

segments.title: Removing stamps from envelopes
segments.summary: Process for soaking stamps off paper: sort first, cut with a margin, float in warm tap water for ten to fifteen minutes, avoid red envelopes, then dry between paper towels under a heavy book.

segments.title: Stamp history: Penny Black, first day ceremonies, and US stamps
segments.summary: Early British stamp history including the Penny Black issued before May 6, first day issues and ceremonies, definitive vs commemorative stamps, Britain omitting its name, and the first US stamps in 1847.

segments.title: Stamp catalogs and famous collectors
segments.summary: The Scott Catalog numbering system and its C prefix for airmail, the Michel Catalog filling gaps, and famous collectors including John Lennon, Patrick Dempsey, Queen Elizabeth II, Sally Ride, Amelia Earhart's pre-sold covers, and FDR's stamp designs.

segments.title: Titanic mail
segments.summary: Brief discussion that the RMS Titanic carried mail, which is believed lost.

segments.title: Inverted Jenny and stamp thefts
segments.summary: The 1918 Inverted Jenny error stamp, how the sheets were printed, the one hundred surviving examples, famous thefts including the McCoy block and the New York Public Library theft, the locket discovery in 2002, and its appearance in Brewster's Millions.

segments.title: Listener mail: heartfelt thanks from Zeneida Johnson
segments.summary: A listener from San Jose, California, writes about relying on the show during the COVID lockdown year.

segments.title: Outro and mailing address
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and invite listeners to send email, encouraging a stamp on the envelope.
